interface.name: zopenlook_workspaces_manager_v1
interface.description:
This protocol lets an unprivileged client (olshell) query and change which OpenLook workspace is active on a given output, and learn which output and workspace a given toplevel belongs to.
Workspaces are per-output (each monitor cycles its own independent sequence, following i3/Sway's convention rather than a single desktop-wide sequence) -- see zopenlook_workspaces_output_v1 for the request/event pair actually scoped to one. This manager is just how a client obtains one of those per output, plus the one thing that necessarily spans all of them: which output a toplevel currently belongs to.
olcore intentionally keeps no OpenLook-specific policy beyond tracking, per output, a linear sequence of workspaces and, for each mapped toplevel (as identified via wlr-foreign-toplevel-management), which output and workspace it belongs to. All workspace UI -- switcher strip, naming, animations -- is olshell's responsibility; this protocol only carries the facts olshell needs to draw it.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by bumping the major version number in the protocol and interface names.

request.name: get_output_workspaces

description.summary: obtain the workspace object for one output

request.description: output must currently be a known output (one the compositor has already advertised via wl_output); violating that sends the no_such_output protocol error and leaves the new object inert (any request on it is ignored).

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys this manager object. Does not affect workspace state, or any zopenlook_workspaces_output_v1 already obtained through it.

entry.name: no_such_output
entry.summary: the object does not name a currently-known output

event.name: toplevel_workspace

description.summary: report a toplevel's output and workspace assignment

event.description: Sent whenever a toplevel is assigned to, or reassigned to, an output and workspace -- including being dragged across an output boundary, which reassigns it to wherever it lands. toplevel is a handle from wlr-foreign-toplevel-management- unstable-v1, letting olshell correlate this assignment with the toplevel metadata (title, app_id, ...) that protocol already provides; index is relative to output's own workspace sequence, not a desktop-wide one.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the output index is relative to

arg.name: index
arg.summary: workspace index the toplevel now belongs to, relative to output

interface.name: zopenlook_workspaces_output_v1

description.summary: linear workspace switching for one output

interface.description: One output's independent workspace sequence -- switching here never affects any other output's active workspace. Obtained via zopenlook_workspaces_manager_v1.get_output_workspaces.

request.name: switch_to

description.summary: activate a workspace on this output

request.description: Requests that the compositor make the workspace at the given index the active one on this object's output. index must be less than the count most recently sent in a workspace_count event; out-of-range values are ignored.

request.name: assign_toplevel

description.summary: move a toplevel to a workspace on this output

request.description: Requests that toplevel (a handle from wlr-foreign-toplevel-management-unstable-v1) be reassigned to the workspace at index on this object's output -- moving it to this output too, if it wasn't already here. index must be less than the count most recently sent in a workspace_count event; out-of-range values are ignored, as is a toplevel handle that doesn't currently name a mapped toplevel. Reassigning a toplevel off the active workspace hides it immediately (and moves focus elsewhere if it had it); reassigning one onto the active workspace shows it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys this object. Does not affect workspace state.

event.name: workspace_count

description.summary: advertise the number of workspaces on this output

event.description: Sent once immediately after creation, and again whenever the number of workspaces on this output changes.

arg.name: count
arg.summary: total number of workspaces on this output

event.name: active_changed

description.summary: advertise the active workspace on this output

event.description: Sent once immediately after creation, and again whenever the active workspace on this output changes, regardless of what caused the change (this client's own switch_to request, another client's, or a compositor-bound keybinding).
